items.title: A sufficiently divisible Veronese subring of a finitely generated graded algebra is generated in degree one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a graded ring S finitely generated over S_0, the lemma states that for all sufficiently divisible d the Veronese subring in degree d is generated in degree one over S_0 (statement lines 13499-13504). The proof does not use Hilbert functions or asymptotic generation theorems: after making the generators homogeneous it describes the monomials of a given degree, takes m to be a common multiple of the generator degrees, and uses a pigeonhole argument to show that every monomial of degree N m with N at least r already contains a monomial of degree m as a factor, which gives generation in degree one for the Veronese subring in degree r m (proof lines 13506-13522). The pigeonhole step and the choice of r m are the content, and the author writes both out. H2.
